THE DOORPLATES: one per room, seen ONLY from above during an era relocation (docs/REINTERP_THE_BUILDING_2026-08-02.md scope item 4). Register: BUILDING SIGNAGE — the flat plate beside a door, the card in a buzzer slot — NOT an exhibition label. So: no dates-of-work, no 'gay teen, 1997', no curatorial voice, nothing that explains the room to you. Each plate carries three fields and no more: `era` (the resident's own year, as a landlord's occupancy card would carry it), `name`, and `line` (the note a person tapes under their own bell). ⚑ THE LAW ON THE LINES: read in sequence the three plates are the piece's thesis and NO SINGLE ONE STATES IT — a plate that said anything about surveillance, isolation or 'other people' would be the frame narrating, which this piece never does. What the sequence does instead is thirty years of one door getting harder to reach: ring twice (come in) → leave it with me (I am always in) → do not call (stop arriving). Nobody explains anything. OPEN FOR SÉRGIO: (a) r3's `era` is the piece's own present as a bare year — 'PRESENT' or an empty field are both live alternatives and both change what the plate is; (b) the plates are STATIC, so Room 1 still reads 1997/DANIEL after the room ages to 2003 and after it is vacated at E3 — a struck-through or blank r1 plate from E3 on is the obvious next beat and is deliberately NOT built, because it would be the piece commenting.
